title: Near-duplicate Cloudflare Media Purger with behavioral drift across packages/storage and tfp-collage-service
evidence: Both files implement identical 100-URL batching, Set-based deduplication, AbortSignal.timeout(10_000), and POST { files: ... } payload to Cloudflare purge endpoint. However, error messages drift: packages/storage throws sentences ('Media purge token is not configured', 'Media purge failed with status ${response.status}') while tfp-collage-service throws uppercase tokens ('CLOUDFLARE_MEDIA_PURGE_TOKEN_NOT_CONFIGURED', 'CDN_PURGE_FAILED:${response.status}'). Collage service also accepts an optional fetchImpl parameter for test injection.
observed_behaviour: Two copies of the same external HTTP integration adapter maintained independently across distinct repositories.
why_it_matters: Changes to Cloudflare API rate limits, batch size constraints, or timeout requirements must be manually applied to both locations. Error handling divergence makes centralized log monitoring inconsistent.
alternative_explanation: Collage service was developed as an isolated microservice before shared contracts between packages were finalized.
recommended_action: Extract CloudflareMediaPurger into a shared contract library or publishable package, supporting optional fetch injection and unified error tokens.
expected_benefit: Single source of truth for CDN cache invalidation logic and consistent observability.
behaviour_preservation_constraints: Collage service test suites injecting mock fetch must be supported; downstream alert filters matching specific error strings must be updated.

title: Duplicate image MIME magic-byte detection across packages/uploads and apps/api
evidence: Both modules implement identical byte signature checking (hasPrefix, JPEG [0xff, 0xd8, 0xff], PNG [0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47], WEBP RIFF/WEBP). Important distinction: detectMimeByMagicBytes in packages/uploads also detects PDF (%PDF-) for document uploads, whereas detectImageMimeType in apps/api contains an explicit byteLength < 4 guard and strictly validates images for moderation.
observed_behaviour: Low-level binary inspection logic duplicated across utility files.
why_it_matters: Adding support for new formats (e.g. AVIF, HEIC) or security patches risks leaving one validator incomplete.
alternative_explanation: API moderation needed a quick lightweight image check without taking a direct dependency on the broader uploads package.
recommended_action: Consolidate binary signature detection in packages/uploads, ensuring the short-buffer (< 4 bytes) guard is preserved and exposing an image-only filter option.
expected_benefit: Single source of truth for MIME spoofing prevention.
behaviour_preservation_constraints: Must preserve short-buffer safety (byteLength < 4) and prevent PDF MIME types from passing image-only validation in moderation.

title: Unused Repository implementations and decoupled Hexagonal persistence architecture
evidence: packages/database/src/repositories/ defines 12 concrete repository classes plus 3 support files. Static analysis reveals that 9 concrete repositories (ContestRepository, ContestSubmissionRepository, EventRepository, OpportunityRepository, MessageRepository, PortfolioImageRepository, ReportRepository, ModerationCaseRepository, PasswordResetTokenRepository) have zero callers anywhere in the codebase. Only 3 concrete repositories have active call sites (UserRepository and OAuthAccountRepository in oauth-user-service.ts; UserViolationRepository in admin-violations-routes.ts). Application commands and queries elsewhere query Prisma directly. Furthermore, regarding soft-deletion: packages/database/src/index.ts softDeleteExtension intercepts root model queries on 11 models, but does NOT intercept nested relation joins (include: { submissions: true }) or raw SQL ($queryRaw/$executeRaw), where explicit deletedAt: null filtering remains required.
observed_behaviour: Nine repository classes sit completely inert in packages/database while the rest of the application executes queries directly through Prisma.
why_it_matters: Cognitive clutter and maintenance overhead. However, retiring unused repositories must not be conflated with abandoning database independence: application commands and queries should own domain interfaces (ports), while Prisma serves as the infrastructure adapter.
alternative_explanation: Repositories were created during an initial architecture pass, but subsequent domain modules implemented direct query/mutation logic.
recommended_action: Safely remove the 9 uncalled concrete repository classes after updating IRepositories and createRepositories in packages/database. For active callers (User, OAuthAccount, UserViolation), retain repository interfaces owned by the domain/application layer and implemented via Prisma adapters. Preserve atomic transaction boundaries covering domain mutations and outbox writes.
expected_benefit: Removes ~1,400 lines of dead code while establishing a clean Hexagonal Ports & Adapters separation for active persistence access.
behaviour_preservation_constraints: Do not force direct Prisma calls on existing repository consumers. Retain explicit deletedAt: null filtering in relation joins and raw queries, as softDeleteExtension does not intercept nested joins. Update createRepositories factory and IRepositories interface to prevent compilation breaks.
risk_of_changing_it: Low for the 9 uncalled repositories once factory is updated; medium for the 3 active repositories requiring interface alignment.

title: Unused createInMemoryRateLimiter and cache adapter location in packages/database
evidence: packages/database/src/adapters/ exports createInMemoryRateLimiter (in rate-limiter.adapter.ts) and createInMemoryCache (in cache.adapter.ts). Full workspace search shows createInMemoryRateLimiter has zero consumers across all files. In contrast, createInMemoryCache is actively consumed in apps/api/src/server.ts:522 for Fastify request caching. However, an in-memory Map-based cache adapter is an application-level infrastructure concern, not a database persistence concern.
observed_behaviour: An unused rate-limiter factory and an in-memory cache utility reside inside the database package adapters directory.
why_it_matters: createInMemoryRateLimiter is dead code. Housing in-memory cache abstractions in packages/database blurs package boundaries and misplaces dependencies.
alternative_explanation: In-memory adapters were placed in packages/database alongside Redis connection stubs during early scaffolding.
recommended_action: Retire the unused createInMemoryRateLimiter export. Relocate createInMemoryCache to apps/api/src/infrastructure/cache/ or packages/shared.
expected_benefit: Eliminates dead code and aligns package responsibilities.
behaviour_preservation_constraints: Preserve createInMemoryCache interface and behavior in apps/api/src/server.ts:522.

title: Eager synchronous disk I/O and potential memory overhead in packages/i18n catalog loading
evidence: packages/i18n/src/index.ts executes loadLanguageCatalogs() synchronously at module evaluation time (line 112). This performs fs.readdirSync and fs.readFileSync across 95 JSON catalog files in catalogs/languages/ totaling 23.95 MB (approx 24 MB) into an in-memory dictionary. Any process importing packages/i18n (API server, background workers, CLI scripts) synchronously parses all 95 languages into heap memory upon startup, regardless of whether a single locale is requested. Canonical fallback locales are en_US (master) and en_IN (default).
observed_behaviour: Top-level synchronous filesystem operations and JSON parsing during module initialization.
why_it_matters: Increases process cold-start latency, memory footprint, and disk contention, particularly in serverless or short-lived CLI environments. However, actual runtime impact must be empirically profiled before asserting specific production savings.
alternative_explanation: Synchronous initialization ensured that catalog lookup was purely synchronous and never required async/await at call sites.
recommended_action: Adopt lazy on-demand locale catalog loading with an in-memory LRU or Map cache, retaining synchronous resolution for pre-loaded fallback locales (en_US, en_IN). Prior to rollout, execute the empirical measurement protocol (recording baseline RSS and startup time vs lazy loading).
expected_benefit: Reduces cold-start I/O and eliminates parsing overhead for unrequested languages.
behaviour_preservation_constraints: Must preserve exact locale fallback rules (regional locale -> base language -> en_US / en_IN) and maintain catalog key parity.
risk_of_changing_it: Medium; requires ensuring callers tolerate asynchronous hydration or that fallback catalogs are pre-warmed synchronously.
open_questions: Measure empirical cold-start delta across API, worker, and Astro SSR runtimes.

title: Monolithic god-object, 4,272-line class and 2,170-line method in tfp-moderation-service
evidence: service.py is 6,162 lines of Python. Class ImageDerivedSignalBuilder spans 4,272 lines (lines 234-4506). A single method, ImageDerivedSignalBuilder.build, spans 2,170 lines (lines 251-2420). It mixes broad safety parsing, CLIP semantic score calculation, contrastive scores, anatomy context, clothing context, garment context, human scene analysis, suggestiveness context, and NudeNet raw exposure scores into an indivisible routine. Furthermore, adapters.py is 2,207 lines of Python containing 20 separate classes including 11 distinct computer vision model adapters (FalconsAi, Marqo, Siglip2, ClipContext, Florence, Owlv2, NudeNet, YoloPrivateParts, YoloSubject, ToxicBert, CTranslate2) and ModelAdapterFactory all in one file.
observed_behaviour: Massive monolithic class and method coordinating entire AI inference feature extraction and signal mapping pipelines.
why_it_matters: Extreme cognitive complexity, high cyclomatic complexity, severe regression risk, and high difficulty in writing targeted unit tests.
alternative_explanation: Grew organically as additional computer vision models and signal extraction rules were integrated into the moderation service.
recommended_action: Decompose ImageDerivedSignalBuilder into cohesive single-responsibility feature extractors: AnatomySignalExtractor, SemanticsSignalExtractor, ExposureSignalExtractor, and DiagnosticBuilder. Split adapters.py into discrete model adapter modules under an adapters/ package. Establish golden evaluation baselines using scripts/eval_192_moderation_service.py before refactoring.
expected_benefit: Dramatically improves maintainability, testability, and isolated benchmarking of individual computer vision models.
behaviour_preservation_constraints: Signal dictionary keys, derived floating-point score values, and diagnostic strings must remain identical to baseline model outputs.
risk_of_changing_it: High; requires regression testing against golden benchmark datasets.

title: Exact duplicate page redirects in Astro Web frontend
evidence: Both files are byte-for-byte identical (SHA-256 327cc44c0ab2...), consisting of 7 lines that redirect to /login using localizePathWithQuery while preserving querystrings.
observed_behaviour: Identical Astro page stubs serving legacy authentication redirects.
why_it_matters: Minor duplication; separate page files add build overhead compared to declarative Astro config redirects.
alternative_explanation: Created as separate file endpoints to satisfy Astro file-system routing conventions.
recommended_action: Consolidate into astro.config.mjs redirects configuration table or retain as explicit routing stubs.
behaviour_preservation_constraints: Querystring parameters (e.g. redirect_to, email) and 302 status code must be preserved.

title: Duplicate appeal creation commands and layer-crossing route import in API
evidence: CreateModerationAppeal in admin-appeal.commands.ts and CreateReportAppeal in report.commands.ts execute 100% identical prisma.moderationAppeal.create mutations with identical schema selection. Furthermore, public moderation routes (moderation-appeal-routes.ts:54) cross module boundaries by importing CreateModerationAppeal from the admin domain.
observed_behaviour: Duplicate command logic and inappropriate architectural coupling between public user routes and admin module commands.
why_it_matters: Violates domain modularity: end-user features depend directly on internal administrative handlers.
alternative_explanation: The appeal feature was initially developed inside admin tooling and later copied into the report module.
recommended_action: Consolidate into a single command owned by apps/api/src/modules/moderation/ or report/, and eliminate the duplicate admin command.
expected_benefit: Removes redundant mutation code and cleans up cross-domain boundary violations.
behaviour_preservation_constraints: Ensure both moderation and report route handlers continue to return the expected ModerationAppeal DTO shape.

title: Boundary-crossing relative imports from test/QA scripts into internal API implementation
evidence: Root architecture verification scripts import internal API modules using deep relative traversals (e.g., ../../apps/api/src/modules/...) instead of using public package exports or HTTP API contracts.
observed_behaviour: Test scripts bypassing module encapsulation to inspect internal implementation files.
why_it_matters: Tightly couples testing/verification scripts to internal file system layout, causing tests to break during routine internal refactoring.
alternative_explanation: Scripts needed to inspect AST structures of routes directly for architecture enforcement.
recommended_action: Scope architectural verification tests to analyze file paths dynamically via AST scanners rather than importing internal TypeScript files directly.
expected_benefit: Decouples test tooling from internal file naming.
behaviour_preservation_constraints: Must ensure architectural compliance checks continue to cover all API route files.

title: Monolithic server bootstrapping and entangled concern registration in apps/api/src/server.ts
evidence: apps/api/src/server.ts spans 790 lines and entangles server creation, Helmet security headers, CORS negotiation, Rate limiting, OpenTelemetry metrics, Prometheus scrapers, Sentry error capturing, in-memory cache initialization, Prisma lifecycle hooks, and manual route registration into a single function. Fastify plugin encapsulation (fastify.register) is underutilized.
observed_behaviour: Single large bootstrap file handling diverse infrastructural and application concerns.
why_it_matters: Testing individual middleware, plugins, or error handlers in isolation is difficult. Fastify route encapsulation and hook inheritance are obscured.
alternative_explanation: Server initialization grew iteratively as production security, telemetry, and rate-limiting requirements were added.
recommended_action: Decompose server.ts into discrete, cohesive Fastify plugins (e.g. securityPlugin, telemetryPlugin, cachePlugin, databasePlugin) using fastify-plugin (fp), strictly preserving lifecycle registration order.
expected_benefit: Improves testability, clarifies lifecycle stages, and allows testing plugins in isolation using fastify.inject().
behaviour_preservation_constraints: Must strictly maintain Fastify hook registration order: telemetry -> security headers -> authentication -> rate limiting -> routes -> error handlers.
risk_of_changing_it: Medium; incorrect plugin order can compromise security header emission or error trapping.

title: Handwritten ES5 duplication of Raw Policy AST Parser and Evaluator in tfp-moderation-service
evidence: browser_policy_evaluator_toolkit.js is a 1,236-line handwritten ES5 JavaScript file embedded into moderation HTML review reports by scripts/run_folder_moderation_audit.py. Lines 650-980 duplicate the recursive descent AST tokenizer, parser (parseOr, parseAnd, parseComparison, parseUnary, parsePrimary), and evaluator from packages/moderation/src/raw-policy/runtime.ts without any generator, build pipeline, or shared contract.
observed_behaviour: Two completely separate codebases (TypeScript in packages/moderation vs handwritten ES5 in Python static files) implementing the same domain expression language.
why_it_matters: High risk of evaluation divergence: if the canonical TypeScript parser adds an operator or changes precedence, offline browser audit reports will produce incorrect policy verdicts compared to the backend.
alternative_explanation: The browser evaluation toolkit was built to allow client-side interactive threshold tuning in self-contained offline HTML reports.
recommended_action: Bundle packages/moderation/src/raw-policy/runtime.ts using esbuild/rollup into an IIFE bundle that is copied or published to the moderation service static assets, replacing the handwritten ES5 implementation.
expected_benefit: Guarantees 100% semantic parity between browser report evaluations and backend moderation scoring.
behaviour_preservation_constraints: The compiled bundle must run in standalone browser environments without external module loaders.

title: Direct shared-database outbox and entity table coupling in tfp-ai-interface worker
evidence: tfp_ai_interface/worker_repository.py connects directly to the monorepo PostgreSQL database using psycopg 3.x and psycopg_pool.ConnectionPool. It polls the event_outbox table using raw SQL with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED row locking. Furthermore, it executes direct raw SQL queries against 7 monorepo domain entity tables (opportunities, events, contests, users, quick_requests, contest_submissions, portfolio_images) to enrich AI prompts, bypassing the Fastify API entirely.
observed_behaviour: An external Python microservice sharing and directly mutating/reading the central transactional database schema.
why_it_matters: Direct database coupling creates cross-repository schema lock-in. Any Prisma migration or column rename in the monorepo will silently break tfp-ai-interface workers at runtime without compilation errors.
alternative_explanation: Direct database polling was chosen to achieve high throughput and eliminate HTTP hop latency for heavy AI background jobs.
recommended_action: Encapsulate entity enrichment queries behind authenticated internal API endpoints or enrich event_outbox payload envelopes with required domain context at dispatch time. If direct outbox polling is retained, define shared schema contracts and automated cross-repository schema verification in CI.
expected_benefit: Prevents uncoordinated database schema migrations from breaking the AI inference pipeline.
behaviour_preservation_constraints: Maintain at-least-once outbox delivery and PostgreSQL FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED concurrency semantics.
risk_of_changing_it: Medium; requires careful coordination between API outbox publishers and AI worker consumers.
open_questions: Evaluate latency impact of HTTP enrichment vs self-contained outbox event payloads.
